Merged into rubric/crosswalk.json only at promotion (after the defender freeze and the single held-out run). Fields and value sets follow rubric/RATING-CODEBOOK.md v1.2.

vectors.name: Unentitled tool call (per-caller function-level authorization)
vectors.description: Several callers (client applications, users, or agents acting for users) share one MCP gateway or server. A caller invokes a tool that the deployment's policy grants to other callers but not to it, or that an explicit deny rule removes from its grant. Without a per-caller, per-tool decision made on every call, any authenticated caller can use every tool the gateway exposes.
vectors.provenance: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023, API5 Broken Function Level Authorization; CWE-862 Missing Authorization and CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization; NIST SP 800-207 §2.1 tenets 3 and 4 (per-session access to each resource, decided by dynamic policy). Distinct from excessive-permission (a privilege the tool or server holds for everyone) and task-authz-bypass (task-ID addressing): here the same call is correct for one caller and wrong for another.
vectors.revisionNotes: Independent of protocol revision. The MCP authorization specification authenticates the client to the server; which tools an authenticated caller may invoke is left to the deployment.

vectors.name: Argument overreach beyond the caller's grant
aliases: broken object level authorization on tool arguments
vectors.description: A caller is entitled to a tool only for some argument values: certain environments, repositories, paths below a directory, or amounts up to a limit. The call uses the tool with a value outside that caller's grant, sometimes encoded to slip past a naive comparison (a '..' path segment, a sibling directory sharing a name prefix, a number sent as a string, a look-alike character). The same value may be legitimately allowed for another caller, so the decision depends on who is calling, unlike a fixed server boundary.
vectors.provenance: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023, API1 Broken Object Level Authorization; CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key; CWE-22 Path Traversal; CWE-1289 Improper Validation of Unsafe Equivalence in Input. Distinct from roots-scope-gap (one fixed filesystem boundary for every caller) and out-of-scope-params (parameters outside the declared schema): here every argument is schema-valid and the boundary is the caller's own grant.
vectors.revisionNotes: Independent of protocol revision; with Roots deprecated in 2026-07-28, argument-level boundaries move into server or gateway configuration, which is where per-caller grants live.

vectors.name: Delegated agent overreach (confused deputy)
aliases: service-account privilege used for a user
vectors.description: An agent calls tools on behalf of a signed-in user. The call should succeed only if both the user and the acting agent are entitled to it. It goes wrong in two directions: the agent uses a tool or argument the user may use but the agent was never granted, or the agent's own broad service grant is used for a user who lacks that entitlement (a confused deputy). Prior agents earlier in a delegation chain are informational and grant nothing.
vectors.provenance: RFC 8693 §1.1 (delegation: the actor acts for the subject with its own identity) and §4.1 (only the current actor is relevant to access control); CWE-441 Unintended Proxy or Intermediary ('Confused Deputy'); OWASP Agentic Top 10 2026 ASI03. Distinct from delegation-chain-laundering, which asks whether the current actor may present tokens to an upstream at all; here the actor is accepted and the question is which tools and arguments it may use for this user.
vectors.revisionNotes: Independent of protocol revision. Identity of the user and the acting agent is assumed already authenticated (by the delegation family's checks or the deployment's identity provider).

vectors.name: Authorization on self-asserted identity
vectors.description: The authenticated caller is not entitled to a call, but the request names a different, entitled principal in a place the caller controls: a tool argument, an HTTP header, request metadata, or an answer to an input request. A gateway or server that authorizes on that asserted identity instead of the authenticated one lets any caller borrow another's privileges.
vectors.provenance: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key; CWE-290 Authentication Bypass by Spoofing; CWE-807 Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision. Distinct from delegation-subject-mixing (several tokens naming different users) and server-impersonation: here exactly one caller is authenticated and the asserted identity is plain request data.
vectors.revisionNotes: Independent of protocol revision. In 2026-07-28 request metadata (_meta) and input responses are additional caller-controlled places an identity can be asserted.
